【Security researchers last week revealed a vulnerability in Apple's iCloud Private Relay feature. While the feature is supposed to protect users' IP addresses from being tracked by visited websites, a flaw means it often fails to do so.】

【Whenever any Apple product or service has an issue, a class action lawsuit almost invariably follows, and this case is no exception……】

【What is iCloud Private Relay?】

【As we explained previously, iCloud Private Relay is not a true VPN, but it is designed with a similar purpose: to prevent your web activity from being tracked while using the Safari browser. Here is Apple's description of its functionality:】

  • 【Your IP address is visible to your network provider and to the first relay, which is operated by Apple. Your DNS records are encrypted, so neither party can see the website address you are trying to visit.】
  • 【The second relay, which is operated by a third-party content provider, generates a temporary IP address, decrypts the name of the website you requested, and connects you to that site.】

【In other words, your ISP only sees that you are connecting to an Apple server, and the website you visit only sees the IP address generated by that server.】

【Where is the vulnerability?】

【Security researchers found that any website that supports passkeys can see your real IP address.】

【What makes it worse is that it doesn't actually matter whether a website truly supports passkeys — merely pretending to support them is enough to leak your IP address.】

【Class action lawsuit】

【Clarkson Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Apple over this, accusing it of false advertising, misrepresentation, and fraud. The firm previously secured a $250 million settlement related to the delayed rollout of Siri AI.】

【Tim Giordano, a partner at Clarkson, told us that the firm considers this a "serious betrayal of consumer trust."】

【We have reached out to Apple for comment and will update this report when we receive a response.】
